title: A chronotropic–ST interaction gives a small, regularization-sensitive cross-center prediction gain
abstract: A frozen Cleveland logistic model (303 patients) was evaluated on 261 complete-case Hungarian patients in the public UCI Heart Disease collection. Adding age-adjusted peak-HR deficit and its interaction with ST depression lowered Brier score from 0.139779 to 0.136194 (difference −0.003585; fixed-model patient-bootstrap 95% interval −0.005494 to −0.001730). Discovery-refit uncertainty spanned −0.017380 to +0.018021; weak regularization reversed the gain and label-shuffle controls undermined specificity. Thus the result is a small model-conditional cross-center gain, not stable incremental physiology, novelty of chronotropic adjustment, or clinical superiority. Inputs, frozen predictions, author formula checks, clean rerun and unfavorable sensitivity results are supplied.
